context_limit: Static matching-version local dependency/generated code is explanatory context, not the downloaded actual CI bundle or an execution of these methods. The actual raw gradle.log and generated runner bundle were not uploaded; original XML/receipt facts remain the actual result evidence. Exact native per-method wall time cannot be recovered from these artifacts.
context_observations: Kotlin test Jasmine/Mocha adapter passes the returned test callback; the filtering/console adapter returns fn() rather than discarding its Promise.
kotlinx-coroutines-test createTestResult returns a native Promise; Mocha detects thenables and completes/fails the test on resolution/rejection.

Karma Kotlin reporter receives a completed result, buffers TestStarted and TestFinished together, and flushes test/suite messages later. It supplies duration but no creation timestamp in those messages.

KGP2.4.20 TCServiceMessagesClient TestStarted/TestFinished uses getTs(message); getTs reads creation timestamp or currentTimeMillis, not TestFinished duration. Buffered messages therefore do not make XML duration a native wall-clock measurement.
purpose: Do not confuse buffered Gradle XML event timing with native browser test duration or infer an asynchronous test defect from milliseconds alone.
